clue.text: Addiction: Hard? Not entirely

blocks.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
'not entirely' means only partly, a bit

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether kicking an addiction is hard, and gets a hedged reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a compulsive, ingrained practice, so an addiction such as a smoking habit fits.

clue.text: Day in sport, running and jumping

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the sport's name

blocks.note: hurling is a fast Irish field game played with sticks
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A day of athletics, all running and jumping.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurling is an Irish stick-and-ball sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurdling is the athletics event of racing while leaping over barriers along the track.

clue.text: One bird pecked another

blocks.note: pecked means bit with the beak
another bird: the tern, a seabird

explanation.surface: One bird attacks another with its beak.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first, and 'another' refers back to it: a second bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading heron-family species known for its booming call.

clue.text: Piquancy in short dance

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: the tango is an Argentine dance

explanation.surface: A brief dance with a bit of spice to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tang is a sharp, distinctive flavour, and piquancy is that pleasantly sharp quality.

clue.text: Main road, one passing through channel

indicators.note: something passing through a waterway sits inside it, so those letters go within the channel

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for road
the Roman numeral for one
a canal is an artificial channel of water

explanation.surface: A main road crossing a canal, as if a highway were bridging a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means chief or principal, as in cardinal rule, which is the sense of main.

clue.text: Melted chocolate drunk without stopping

indicators.note: melted things lose their shape and reform, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drinking melted chocolate nonstop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the anagram signal; it is part of the fodder, and 'Melted' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Around the clock is an idiom for all day and all night, continuously.

clue.text: Score tied in the end, bet off

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the preceding word
off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: final letter of tied
taken as written

explanation.surface: A match ends level, so the wager is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a match result; here it is an account owed, as in settling a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A score was once a tally of money owed, so a debt is a score to be settled.

clue.text: Old place of birth outlined in note

indicators.note: something outlined is surrounded by a border, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: natal means relating to birth
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: An ancient birthplace recorded in a note.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur is the crosswords' favourite old city, traditionally Abraham's birthplace, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a natural is a note that is neither sharp nor flat, or the sign cancelling one.

clue.text: House and home of a sport

blocks.note: first meaning: the upper chamber of the UK Parliament
second meaning: the London cricket ground

explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is the UK's upper parliamentary chamber; Lord's is the London cricket ground known as the home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the parliamentary chamber and the famous cricket venue share the same name.

clue.text: Extraordinary fat Austrian composer, a pain

blocks.note: flab is excess body fat
Alban Berg, the Austrian composer of Wozzeck
taken as written
a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: An insult about an overweight Austrian composer who is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabbergasting means astonishing, so stunning as to seem remarkable.

clue.text: Describing thin walls of cells, metal inside concrete

indicators.note: inside tells us one word's letters are placed within the other's

blocks.note: concrete in the sense of actual, tangible
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A building description: thin cell walls with metal reinforcement set in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests prison cells and building materials; the cells are in the eye, and concrete means real.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the thin layer of light-sensitive cells lining the back of the eye, so retinal is the adjective describing it.

clue.text: Huge metal object in space, gold tooth?

blocks.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
a tooth is, playfully, something that bites

explanation.surface: A huge lump of metal in space, perhaps a gold tooth gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiter is a spacecraft that circles a planet, a large metal craft travelling in space.

clue.text: Right story ending in redemption

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
final letter of redemption

explanation.surface: A story that ends with redemption is the right one to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Wave by one jetty?

indicators.note: to wave something is to move it about, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wave breaking against a single jetty at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: The jetty is not a pier: read it as jet-like, coloured like jet, the black gemstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony and jet are both proverbially deep black, so something ebony is jet-coloured.

clue.text: God accommodated in secular establishment

indicators.note: accommodated in means housed within, so the word sits inside the run of letters

blocks.note: spans the end of secular and the start of establishment

explanation.surface: A deity given lodging in a secular institution, an irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war.

clue.text: Shawl nicked

blocks.note: first meaning: a long scarf or wrap
second meaning: took without permission

explanation.walkthrough: Nicked is British slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a wrap worn over the shoulders; the verb is the past tense of steal.

clue.text: Go to pay for drinks, and cry

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's turn to buy a round
second meaning: a loud call

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a noun, a turn: in Britain and Australia 'it's my shout' means it's my turn to buy the round.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a turn at buying drinks and a loud call or yell.

clue.text: Pub of course?

blocks.note: surface reading: an obvious pub, 'of course' meaning naturally
setter's reading: the bar belonging to a golf course, the drinking spot after the eighteen holes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like an interjection; it means belonging to a golf course, whose round has eighteen holes, so the bar counts as one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers' slang names the clubhouse bar after a round as the extra hole following the eighteenth.

clue.text: Spook just haunting wetland

indicators.note: a ghost haunting a place lurks inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a fen is low marshy land
just in the sense of fair, morally right

explanation.surface: A ghost simply haunting a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spook' and 'haunting' suggest a ghost noun; Spook is a verb, to scare.
explanation.definitionFit: To spook someone is to startle or scare them.

clue.text: French port in Grenoble unavailable at first, so rum drunk

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the preceding word only
drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
opening letter of unavailable
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: In Grenoble the rum ran out at first, so drinkers had to go elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Grenoble is a French city too, so it looks like part of the definition, but it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Boulogne-sur-Mer is a ferry and fishing port on France's Channel coast.

clue.text: Pane spattered with oil, whitish glass

indicators.note: spattered means splashed about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A window pane splashed with oil, smearing the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline is a milky, translucent glass that resembles opal.

clue.text: Chap defending conflict, the bane of office workers?

indicators.note: a defender surrounds and shields what it protects, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a chap is a man, a male
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A man standing up for a conflict, a pest to workers in an office.
explanation.definitionFit: Malicious software such as viruses plagues computer users at work, so it is fairly called their bane.

clue.text: Grey matter, that which is usually brown or white

definitions.text: that which is usually brown or white

blocks.note: first meaning: the brain, from rhyming slang ... of bread = head

blocks.clueFragment: that which is usually brown or white
blocks.note: second meaning: a baked unit of bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British for 'use your head', from rhyming slang loaf of bread = head.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread comes as a brown or white loaf, and the slang sense makes the word mean brain.

clue.text: Insect briefly circles top of tall flower

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
to circle something is to surround it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a louse is a small parasitic insect
first letter of tall

explanation.surface: A bug flies round the top of a tall bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, a sacred flower in Asian traditions.

clue.text: Song priest sang at Latin Mass, originally

indicators.note: originally points to how each word begins, so the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A priest sings a chant during an old Latin Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the biblical Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Pest shot

blocks.note: first meaning: the garden mollusc that eats plants
second meaning: a gulp of spirits, or a bullet

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pest being shot; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is both a slimy garden pest and a mouthful of liquor or a bullet.

clue.text: Report in good time?

blocks.note: first meaning: a loud deep sound like a gun's report
second meaning: a period of economic prosperity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a written account; it is the bang of a gun. The question mark flags that 'good time' means prosperous times.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a resonant bang and also a period of rapid economic growth.

clue.text: Ambush in district after uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising goes from bottom to top, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a part of town is a district

explanation.surface: An ambush in some district following a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a trap laid for an enemy, a surprise attack from hiding.

clue.text: Power in three leaders in Luxembourg and Italian capital

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the following word
the leaders of words are their opening letters, so those are kept

blocks.note: a trio is a group of three
P is the physics symbol for power
opening letters of Luxembourg and Italian

explanation.surface: A power struggle among three European leaders and an Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Fruit course delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered aloud, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a current is a course or flow of water

explanation.surface: A dessert course of fruit brought to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a meal course; it is a flow, as in the current of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant is a small dried grape or a berry such as blackcurrant, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Crew visiting guru in days gone by

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a sage is a wise teacher
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A crew calls on a wise teacher long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of steam railways and engines is now history, a period of the past.

clue.text: Tidy feathers on entering coop

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a pen is an enclosure like a coop
RE means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A hen tidies its feathers upon going into the coop.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom their plumage with the beak, which is what preening means.
